Q: How to structure a database with questions and answers? A:

The barrier I discovered is that evidence-based practices (EBP) may not apply the same way in every situation without considering other factors that come with real-life and often complex patient care. While EBP provides strategies for and recommended care, factors such as cultural beliefs, language barriers, and family involvement must also be considered when applying it in practice.

I have encountered several scenarios where I provided education and reinforced patient education, but one that stood out to me involved a patient who needed emergency surgery. Despite the surgeon explaining through an interpreter that the procedure was necessary to save the patient’s life, the husband hesitated to sign the consent papers without first receiving approval from his wife’s family. He feared being blamed if the surgery was unsuccessful. Although he eventually signed the consent, the delay could have been fatal. According to Alatawi et al. (2020), lack of understanding of evidence-based interventions can be a barrier to implementing EBP. In this situation, I believe the husband’s limited understanding of the evidence-based intervention affected his confidence and ability to make a timely decision.

A partial answer, which had the great merit of getting the Application working properly again, was to follow the suggestions of some of the commentors and use SQL Server to host the data which had been kept in the Access database. I have also filed a problem report with the Visual Studio folks, but experience strongly suggests that they, like the mills of God, grind very slowly!

Installing and switching to SQL server for this database was not quite as much of a pain as I expected - nor was making the necessary changes in the Application, and it is now back up and running correctly again.
